title: vCraft first release build spec
description:
## Problem Statement

The vCraft team has completed eight decision tickets that resolve scope, domain model, approval/access rules, journals, quotation workflows, visual direction, technical architecture, and demo acceptance. The codebase has working prototypes and a monorepo with domain packages, contracts, API, frontend, and worker layers. The team now needs one unified implementation brief that names the entry seams for testing, establishes what each tier owns, and confirms the acceptance checks before build starts.

## Solution

Synthesize the eight resolved decisions into a single build spec that defines:
- One test seam per major workflow (guest QR-to-visit, buyer quotation, household publish, admin coordination)
- Module boundaries and owned responsibilities
- API contracts and state machines to keep or change
- Media and notification pipelines
- Demo acceptance matrix tied to grading criteria
- Deployment and fallback setup

The spec treats the domain rules, state machines, and tour sequences as verified from the prior decisions and focuses on implementation seams, concurrency invariants, and observable evidence.

## User Stories

1. As a QA engineer, I want to know the exact entry point for testing each guest/buyer/household/admin journey, so I can build repeatable e2e scenarios on the deployed URL.

2. As a backend engineer, I want to know which state machines stay unmodified and which need new transitions for decline-cascade, decline-cancels-order, and production cancellation, so I can update the domain layer without guessing.

3. As a frontend engineer, I want to know the polling intervals and what each TanStack Query refetch should trigger, so I can build the reactive UI without SSE.

4. As an infrastructure engineer, I want to know the demo database reset boundaries, Supabase connectivity fallbacks, and mail provider setup, so I can prepare the VPS and document the venue setup.

5. As the team lead, I want acceptance checks for Lighthouse, responsive, concurrency, database independence, and upload performance tied to frozen demo data, so I know exactly what to show in the defense and how long each check takes.

6. As a contract owner, I want to know which Zod schemas need to be added or changed for the narrowed quotation flow (no auto-allocation, manual division, whole-order cancellation), so I can sync frontend and backend on request/response shapes.

7. As a household representative in the UI, I want the publish-and-journal path to be testable from a phone in the e2e suite, so the demo script can show the complete household workflow.

8. As a media engineer, I want to know the exact worker job scope (image convert, QR render, outbox relay) and the MIME/size validation boundary, so I can scope the pipeline without overbuilding.

9. As a domain expert, I want the RFQ state machine transitions documented for the new rules (buyer cancellation before production, admin cancellation after production, decline cascade, no reassignment), so I can verify the machine against the resolved spec.

10. As an administrator in the demo, I want the coordination flow to show how to assemble a cooperative quotation from household contributions, confirm allocations, and mark receipt, so the script covers the admin journey end-to-end.

11. As a test architect, I want the seams between domain unit tests, API integration tests, and e2e scenarios defined, so I know where to put each check (unit: state machine races, integration: DB concurrency, e2e: UI flow).

12. As a developer, I want to know which ADR decisions are kept vs. narrowed (e.g., Redis/BullMQ narrowed to three jobs, SSE deferred, assistant removed), so I don't build features that are out of scope.

13. As a grading examiner, I want the acceptance matrix to show one row per journey step with what I see on screen and which role is acting, so I can follow the demo script and check off each requirement.

14. As a performance engineer, I want the demo pre-checks (Lighthouse 90+, zero full reloads, WCAG AA, 360–1440 responsive, 12 MB upload → 1.5 MB output) tied to frozen data and scripts, so I know what baseline to hit before exam day.

15. As a database engineer, I want the MySQL independence tests in CI and the compose mysql profile documented, so the team can verify portability without manual setup.

## Implementation Decisions

### Scope Summary (from vCRAFT-9hg.1, 9hg.7)

Release boundary: Live demo early January 2027, 3-person team, one VPS + Supabase free tier. Complete guest, buyer, household, and admin journeys with Bat Trang sample data. Deferred: full bilingual authoring, fox assistant, 3D/scroll story/advanced motion, MFA enforcement, CAPTCHA, multi-device sessions, price charts, outage banners, QR label PDFs, tour routing, ratings, reallocation. Retained: email verification, password recovery, role checks, artisan invite, lock, audit log, notifications, structured news, household map with text list, production journals with corrections, quotation requests, sealed offers, manual order split, progress tracking, concurrency safety.

### Domain Model (from vCRAFT-9hg.2)

Household: craft-producing unit under own public name. One designated representative account per household (may be artisan or administrator, not a maker by account action). Artisan: individual maker; named artisans need no account for credit. Product: identifies one object or one production batch, own journal and QR code. Workshop: physical location under household; map inclusion ≠ visitor permission. Production batch: objects of one design in one run, one product with shared journal and QR.

### Approval & Access (from vCRAFT-9hg.3)

Four separate claims: Household approval (gate to exhibition and quotation; does not mean sentences true or named artisans made objects). Certificate verification (admin reviewed one certificate; never appears unverified; not proof of genuineness). Journal integrity (published account not silently rewritten; events may not have happened as written). Physical authenticity (never claimed). Actors: guest (no account, public pages), buyer (registered, own quotations), household representative (one account for one household, not made maker), administrator (sample data, not household member). One role per account. Failure: rejection (nothing public), suspension (hides public profile/products/workshops, QR shows unavailable notice, private records stay visible), withdrawal (hides one product and journal), locking representative (freezes journals, published pages stay).

### Production Journals (from vCRAFT-9hg.4)

Entry: one stage, declared date, note, optional images. System records save time (ordering) and declared date (story). Fixed stages: clay, throw, dry, paint, glaze, fire, finish; may repeat or skip (skip requires reason). Corrections: append-only after publication; mistake fixed by new entry naming superseded entry; original and correction shown together. Hash chain: SHA-256 append-only kept. Detects change/deletion/reordering. Does not prove events happened or who made object. QR page states "Journal integrity" label only. Publication: appears only with published product, withdrawn with it. Unfinished may publish (labeled "in progress"). Invalid code, unpublished, withdrawn, or suspended household all return missing page.

### Quotation & Coordination Rules (from vCRAFT-9hg.5)

Quotation lifecycle: Buyer invites selected households, requests admin coordination, or both. Request requires design, positive quantity, unit, destination, required delivery, quotation deadline. Drafts editable; sent specs/dates fixed. Changes require cancellation and replacement. Deadline is any future time (no 24-hour minimum); required delivery follows. Acceptance checks version (refuses stale). Creates order awaiting allocation confirmations. Offers: one offer covers full quantity. Partial goes through cooperative assembled by assigned admin. Each invited household declares max quantity, unit price, promised date; no cross-request reservation. Admin composes within limits; cannot rewrite. Buyer sees households, shares, dates, one complete price. Internal prices private. Allocation and production: all confirm before production starts. Manual division table. Inadequate capacity prevents sending. One household starts direct; assigned admin starts cooperative. Representative reports completed quantity (zero to allocated), notes/photos. Allocation DONE requires full quantity. All DONE permits buyer or admin receipt. After production starts, only admin cancels unfulfillable order. Lateness keeps IN_PRODUCTION. Allocation decline cancels whole unstarted order. State machines: RFQ DRAFT→SENT→BIDDING→ACCEPTED→IN_PRODUCTION→DELIVERED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED. Quotation SUBMITTED→ACCEPTED|REJECTED|WITHDRAWN|LAPSED (with versions). Allocation PROPOSED→CONFIRMED|DECLINED→IN_PROGRESS→DONE|CANCELLED. Changes: rfq-state-machine add buyer cancellation before production, admin cancellation after start, decline-cascade. bid-state-machine retain revision/terminal, enforce via application. allocation-state-machine decline ends own AND triggers whole-order cancel.

### Exhibition Journey (from vCRAFT-9hg.6)

Variant A (market-wall base): continuous reading household → makers → object → journal → visiting → wholesale. Variant C (QR-first guest): seal/journal newest first, walk back to household and visiting with home link. Content order: household history, maker credit, object, evidence, visit, wholesale inquiry. Public news by household, not price grid. Maker credit: individual names; person posting is administration, not maker. Map: real map preferred; text list as accessible alternative. Motion: seal moment + short transitions, respects reduced-motion. 3D hero/scroll story out. Sample data labeled. Open fix: desktop/tablet spacing in A and C needs pass; vase-plate overlap must be verified gone.

### Technical Architecture (from vCRAFT-9hg.7)

ADRs 13-15 stand: Supabase Auth, Storage over S3, business Postgres, pgvector. Browser talks Supabase direct only for sign in/refresh/MFA. All business data through API. No Data API touches business tables. MySQL portability: dual-driver entities, CI tests on MySQL via Testcontainers, compose mysql profile. Postgres-only SQL in supabase migrations only. Contracts own boundary: Zod validates both sides, generates OpenAPI. Controllers thin. /api/v1, cursor pagination, RFC 9457, ETag on reads, version-checked writes, idempotency keys. Optimistic versioning: accept-bid and confirm-allocation in one transaction checking version; stale refused. Deployment: one VPS + Supabase. Caddy TLS and same-origin routing. VPS: web, api, worker, Redis. Supabase: Auth, Postgres, Storage. Local storage fallback. Package boundaries enforced: domain free of framework/ORM/workspace, web never imports database/api, UI no business logic. Media: worker (sharp) converts to AVIF/WebP, renders QR PDFs; API validates magic/size/MIME; stores per ADR-14. Notifications: in-app + email (SMTP). Mail is environment detail. Redis/BullMQ: three jobs (media, mail, outbox relay). Polling (TanStack Query). Reused: hash chain code, MapLibre, auth boundary. Removed: assistant module/Claude/Voyage at runtime (migrations stay), TipTap (plain text + sanitization), weather.

### Demo Setup (from vCRAFT-9hg.8)

Services: one VPS + Caddy + Supabase (Auth, Postgres, Storage). Cloudflare Tunnel backup. SMTP mail (no SDK). Sample: one buyer, one household rep, one admin, one pending. ~20 households, 200+ products (4–7 stages), 12 quotation requests across states, one split order across 4 households in production, 15+ news. One QR on real cup. Three pre-logged profiles: buyer, household (phone), admin. Demo sequence: QR scan → household approval/publish → workshop discovery → news → buyer quoting → admin coordination → allocation confirms → progress → receipt. Acceptance matrix: one row per step (step, what examiner sees, role). Checks (frozen data): Lighthouse 90+ on key pages, zero full reloads, WCAG AA, responsive 360–1440, keyboard-only QR path, 12 MB upload → 1.5 MB output, concurrency (two-tab race refused with error), database independence (CI Postgres+MySQL), backup/restore practiced. Safety: pnpm demo:reset refuses dev/prod, if external down show local + tunnel first.

## Testing Decisions

Unit tests (packages/domain/test): State machine transitions for new buyer cancellation before production, admin cancellation after start, decline-cascade (whole order). Allocation plan: no cross-request reservation, manual table exact coverage. Hash chain kept.

Integration tests (apps/api/test): Outbox concurrency expands to new events. Supabase guard verifies new actions. New test: two simultaneous accept-bid or confirm-allocation refused with STALE_VERSION. Database independence: CI matrix Postgres + MySQL (Testcontainers).

E2e tests (tests/e2e/specs): Guest (QR → trace → household → map+list → visit). Buyer (request → deadline → expiry → invite → bid → accept → confirm → progress → receipt). Household (login → publish → journal correction visible → approve). Admin (coordinate → assemble → manual table → confirm shares → start → progress → receipt). Seams: guest public page, buyer /buyers, household /studio (phone), admin /admin.

Pre-exam checks: Lighthouse 90+, responsive, keyboard, image upload compress, concurrency race, DB switch to MySQL, backup/restore practiced.

## Out of Scope

Social networks, real household pilot, retail/payments/shipping/invoicing/mobile apps, automatic allocation/Gantt/lateness/reassignment, 3D/scroll/assistant/bilingual, deliverable deployment/live identity/mid-release migrations.

## Further Notes

All eight decisions closed. Spec synthesizes into one build brief. Domain rules and journeys verified from prior decisions, not re-negotiated. Focus on entry seams, module ownership, concurrency, observable checks. Pre-exam checks on frozen demo data, not live guarantees. Demo script repeatable; external outage falls back to local build.

title: vCraft digital exhibition: product specification and technical direction
description:
## Destination

Agree a product specification and technical direction for the first usable vCraft release, a deployed INT3306 digital exhibition with representative sample data, working authentication, saved data, and complete journeys for the required roles. The map is finished when its decision tickets leave a clear implementation brief and no unresolved scope or architecture decisions.

## Notes

See existing map notes; unchanged by this session.

## Decisions so far

- Set the first-release scope and demonstration priorities /vCRAFT-9hg.1: Early Jan 2026 demo, 3 people, one VPS plus Supabase free tier. Complete guest, buyer, household, and admin journeys with Bat Trang sample data. Defer bilingual authoring, fox assistant, 3D/scroll story, and extra account/operations features.
- Define the household, maker, workshop, and product model /vCRAFT-9hg.2: Multiple makers and workshops per household, one representative account, and product identity per object or production batch with its own QR history.
- Define approval, publishing, and access rules /vCRAFT-9hg.3: One role per account; separate claims for approval, certificate verification, journal integrity, and no physical-authenticity claim; audience rules with an unavailable notice for old QR links.
- Define production journals and traceability guarantees /vCRAFT-9hg.4: Append-only after publication with visible correction entries, fixed seven-stage vocabulary with repeats and explained skips, declared date plus system time, the existing hash chain kept with a fixed one-sentence integrity limit, and the corrected failure table where locking freezes but does not hide.
- Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules /vCRAFT-9hg.5: One complete accepted offer, private household contributions, validated manual allocation, confirmations before production, quantity progress and explicit receipt; one strict deadline and whole-order cancellation instead of reassignment.
- Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction /vCRAFT-9hg.6: A (market-wall reading) as base plus C (QR-first entry) for guests; confirmed content order; real map kept with text list as companion; closed-workshop card dropped; desktop and tablet spacing still need a pass before build.

• Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries /vCRAFT-9hg.7: ADRs 13-15 kept without reversal; narrowed worker, polling instead of SSE, MapLibre kept with heavy frontend dropped, hash chain and domain rules reused as is, optimistic versioning, in-app plus email notifications; assistant runtime, TipTap, and weather leave the release.
- [Define the deployed demo and release acceptance checks](vCRAFT-9hg.8): VPS plus Supabase demo with fixed accounts and Bat Trang sample data, one repeatable QR-to-delivery script, and pre-exam evidence for Lighthouse, responsive, upload, concurrency, independence, and recovery.

## Not yet specified

- Further decisions that retained optional features may introduce. First decide whether the features belong in the release before planning their details.
- Focused compatibility or service-limit investigations that may become necessary when the actual architecture alternatives are clear.
- Conflicts between the exhibition prototype, the final content set, and the intended demonstration experience that only become visible after those choices.

## Out of scope

- Social-network features such as follows, public comments, and a social feed. The agreed public experience is a digital exhibition; a later change in direction needs a new scoped effort.
- A pilot with real households and live wholesale orders. This release targets the course demonstration using representative sample data.
- Retail checkout, online payments, shipping integrations, electronic invoicing, and native mobile applications.
- Delivering the application, deploying services, collecting real identity documents, or executing database changes during this planning effort. Small local prototypes are allowed only to support a decision.
- Automatic allocation strategies, global capacity scheduling/reservations, Gantt charts, predicted lateness, and household reassignment are outside first-release coordination, as scoped in Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules /vCRAFT-9hg.5.
notes: Tracker operations, including the verified fallback for contributor routing, are documented in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md under Wayfinding operations. Shared vocabulary starts at root GLOSSARY.md. The user-approved charting scope is recorded by [Chart the vCraft product direction and first-release decision map](vCRAFT-clc).

## Resolution — human accepted Rounds 1-2, 29 Oct 2026

Grilling type. All twelve questions accepted as recommended.

### Service choices
- Demo runs on one VPS behind Caddy for TLS, with Supabase for auth, Postgres, and Storage. Cloudflare Tunnel plus local build stays as venue-network backup only.
- Mail uses environment SMTP. No provider SDK in the codebase.

### Sample data and accounts
- Fixed demo accounts: one buyer, one household representative, one village administrator, plus one pending household.
- Sample volume: about 20 Bat Trang households, 200 plus products with 4-7 journal stages each, 12 quotation requests across all states, one shared order split across 4 households in production, 15 plus news items.

### Demonstration sequence
- Single repeatable script on the deployed URL: real-phone QR scan, household approval and publication, workshop discovery with map plus text list, news, quoting, admin coordination, allocation confirmations, quantity progress through delivery and receipt.
- Shows saved data and permitted versus forbidden actions live, not local simulations.

### Acceptance matrix
- One row per journey step: step, what the examiner sees on screen, performing role. Covers guest QR scan, buyer quoting, household approval and publishing, admin coordination, delivery progress.

### Evidence checks (all run before exam day on frozen data)
- Lighthouse 90 plus on key pages, zero full reloads in the script, capped image variants with lazy loading, WCAG 2.2 AA.

- Database independence: passing CI matrix run on Postgres and MySQL. No mid-defense database switch.
- Recovery: documented demo database backup before exam day plus one practiced restore to a scratch database. No live restore during the defense.

- `pnpm demo:reset` runs only against the demo database URL, refuses development or production targets, restores the exact accounts and records above.

## Question

Distinguish an installed dependency from an implemented integration. Compare alternatives only where a requirement, operational burden, or demonstrated constraint gives a concrete reason.

Resolve authoritative storage and authentication boundaries, API and shared-contract ownership, transactions and concurrency for quotations, media processing and access, notifications needed by the retained workflows, and the database independence required by the course. Address how the frontend hash-chain code and existing pure domain rules should be reused. Account for map, editor, animation, and AI dependencies according to the decisions that retained or excluded them.

Read ADRs 13-15 and the architecture decision summary. Record any accepted reversal explicitly; do not silently override Supabase choices or the MySQL portability obligation. If a decision depends on facts outside the repository, create a focused research ticket and leave that part unresolved until evidence arrives. The answer should specify responsibilities, reuse boundaries, and justified trade-offs with no implementation or migration execution.

Together with their prerequisite resolutions, these establish the behavior the architecture must support. The installed stack is a starting point, not a requirement to use every dependency.

comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted Q1-Q18 through three grilling rounds. No reversals of ADRs 13-15. No research tickets needed: every decision rested on repo facts or prior resolutions.

### Kept as specified (no change)

- ADRs 13, 14, 15 stand. Supabase keeps Auth, Storage over S3, business Postgres, and pgvector. Browser talks to Supabase directly only for sign in, refresh, and MFA. All business data goes through the API. No Data API access touches business tables. MySQL portability stays a tested obligation: dual-driver entities and migrations, CI integration tests on MySQL via Testcontainers, compose mysql profile for local checks. Postgres-only SQL lives only in supabase migrations.
- Contracts own the API boundary. Zod schemas validate both sides and generate the OpenAPI document. Controllers stay thin: map entities to DTOs, hold no business logic.
- Optimistic versioning for acceptance races. Accept-bid and confirm-allocation run in one transaction checking a version column; stale writes are refused. No pessimistic locks at demo scale.
- Deployment is one VPS plus Supabase. Caddy terminates TLS and routes same-origin traffic. VPS runs web, api, worker, Redis. Supabase hosts Auth, Postgres, Storage. Local storage driver is the offline demo fallback only.
- Package boundaries are enforced in CI via dependency-cruiser per ARCHITECTURE 3.2. Domain stays free of framework, ORM, and workspace imports. Web never imports database or api code. UI knows no business logic.
- API conventions stay as specified: /api/v1, cursor pagination, RFC 9457 problems, ETag on public reads, version-checked writes, idempotency keys on state-changing POSTs.
- Mail is an environment detail. SMTP settings come from the environment behind a mail port. Mailpit for dev, VPS SMTP for demo. No provider SDK in the codebase.

### Kept with narrowed scope

- Redis, BullMQ, and the worker stay, scoped to three jobs: media processing, mail delivery, outbox relay. Redis holds no durable data and runs locally on the VPS. The API never does image conversion, PDF rendering, or SMTP sends inline. SSE hub and Redis pub/sub wiring leave the release.
- Live updates use polling. TanStack Query refetch covers offer arrival, allocation confirmation, and progress reports. SSE is deferred.
- Media pipeline runs in the worker with sharp. API validates magic bytes, size, MIME at the boundary. Worker converts to AVIF/WebP, renders QR label PDFs, stores per ADR-14 bucket rules.
- MapLibre stays because the journey decision retained the real map with a text-list companion. R3F hero, GSAP scroll story, and Motion transitions leave the release.
- Hash chain code reused as is. Domain chain logic and the frontend verification copy stay where they are. Backend verifies on journal write, browser re-verifies on public display.
- Notifications are in-app plus email only. Quotation events write an in-app row and queue SMTP mail. No SMS, push, or digest.
- Auth boundary stays as drawn. Supabase owns identity, sessions, refresh, MFA, OAuth. API verifies JWTs via JWKS, enforces RBAC plus resource policies, requires MFA for admin, checks lockout per request. No local passwords.

### Removed from the release

- Assistant stack: no assistant module, no Claude API calls, no Voyage embeddings at runtime. ADR-13 migrations stay so the knowledge table and RPC exist, but nothing reads or writes them.
- TipTap: admin news is plain text with server-side sanitization. Editor dependencies leave the web app.
- Weather: Open-Meteo integration dropped. Nothing retained needs it.

### Out of scope (confirmed, not decided away here)

- Automatic allocation strategies, Gantt, predicted lateness (already excluded by 9hg.5).
- 3D/scroll storytelling, fox assistant, bilingual authoring (already deferred by 9hg.1).

title: Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules
description:
## Question

What complete quotation and shared-order journeys must the Buyer, Artisan, and village Admin be able to carry out, and which rules determine valid progress?

Reconcile the assignment, the detailed SRS, and the implemented RFQ, Bid, and Allocation state machines. Work through both a single-household quote and the assignment example of 5,000 custom cups shared among households. Decide how invitations and capacity work, how quotations stay private, when offers may change or expire, how acceptance creates an order, and how households confirm and report their allocated work through delivery.

Resolve necessary exception behavior, including concurrent acceptance, a household declining an allocation, inadequate capacity, cancellation, and reassignment, at the level required by the agreed release scope. Determine which proposed allocation strategies and progress displays are justified. Keep payment and shipping integrations outside the boundary. The answer should establish states, invariants, responsibilities, and concrete scenarios; it should not implement controllers or extend the existing machines without a decision.
notes: Prerequisite: [Define approval, publishing, and access rules](vCRAFT-9hg.3). Read its resolution and the linked scope and identity decisions before working this question.
close_reason: Quotation, coordination, privacy, lifecycle and failure rules agreed through Q1-Q13; resolution and source handoff recorded

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q1 and Q2. Each quotation request ends in at most one accepted offer covering its full requested quantity. A household may offer the whole quantity; a household that can supply only part contributes through a cooperative offer assembled by the assigned village administrator. The buyer compares complete offers and does not independently accept fragments of competing offers. The buyer explicitly invites one or several approved households. A separate opt-in shares the request with the assigned administrator for village coordination; that administrator may invite additional households to contribute. There is no automatic broadcast to all households. Existing private-audience rules and the scope deferral of reassignment remain in force. This ticket remains in progress; lifecycle, capacity, pricing, acceptance, allocation confirmation, progress, and exception rules still need live discussion.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q3 and Q4. Before sending, a request requires the actual design/customisation, quantity, delivery destination, required delivery date, and one quotation deadline. A product page may be a design reference; optional notes and images explain the work. Requested terms are fixed after sending. A material change requires cancelling and replacing the request so households never quote against different specifications. The quotation deadline governs both submission and acceptance and is separate from required delivery. A current quotation is available until the deadline unless its author withdraws or replaces it. Before acceptance the author may submit a revision; private history retains prior versions. Acceptance must name the current version and refuses a stale version after a price change. These declarations do not reserve capacity across other requests. Admin may compose an offer only within each households declared quantity, price, and date, and cannot rewrite its contribution. comments.text: Discussion checkpoint: the human accepted Q8-Q10. A household declining a proposed allocation cancels the whole unstarted order, preserves quotation/allocation history, and notifies participants; no silent substitution. Before production the buyer or an administrator can cancel the whole order with a required reason. A confirmed household requests administrator cancellation rather than silently withdrawing. Inadequate capacity prevents sending a cooperative quote; the request stays open until deadline or buyer cancellation. The sole household starts a direct order; the assigned admin starts a cooperative order after all allocations confirm. Each representative reports completed quantity bounded from zero to allocated quantity, optional notes/photos, and corrections retaining the earlier report with a required reason. Buyer/admin see household progress and a quantity-weighted overall percentage. A table shows promised dates and flags overdue unfinished shares. Gantt and predicted-lateness displays are excluded. Progress is private and does not automatically create/publish production journals. After production starts only an administrator may cancel an unfulfillable whole order with a required reason; completed quantities/history remain, unfinished allocations cancel, and the order is CANCELLED, never DELIVERED. comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted Q1-Q13 and confirmed this shared first-release specification. GLOSSARY.md records the vocabulary.

### Requests and offers

- A verified buyer invites selected approved households, requests village coordination, or does both. Coordination alone is valid. One assigned administrator may invite more households. No automatic broadcast, ranked matching or automatic coordination escalation.
- Require design/customisation, positive whole-number quantity, unit, destination, required delivery and quotation deadline. Notes/images are optional. All shares use the same unit. Referencing a product does not reserve or redefine its batch or stock.
- The quotation deadline is any future time, without a 24-hour minimum. Required delivery follows it. Offered completion dates fall after that deadline and on or before required delivery.
- Drafts are editable. Sent specifications and dates are fixed; changes require cancellation and a replacement request using the old details.
- Submission, revision, withdrawal and acceptance require now strictly before the same deadline. Every unaccepted request expires then, with or without offers. There is no seven-day acceptance extension, even if expiry processing runs late.
- The buyer accepts one current, complete quotation covering the full quantity. Revisions retain private history. Stale versions cannot be accepted. Acceptance fixes terms, creates one order and proposed allocations, and rejects competing active quotations.

### Coordination, capacity and privacy

- A household contribution offer states its own maximum quantity for this request, unit price and completion date. Partial contributions go to the administration, not into independently accepted buyer orders. Declared availability does not reserve capacity across requests; no global scheduling or double-booking guarantee is promised.
- The administrator plans manually using households, quantities, prices and dates. Sending requires exact full coverage, positive integer shares within household offers, unchanged household rates, and valid dates. Inadequate capacity prevents sending; the request stays open until cancellation or deadline.
- Changing or withdrawing an input contribution withdraws any dependent unaccepted cooperative quotation and notifies buyer/coordinator. The administrator must check current inputs and issue a new version. Accepted contributions and plans cannot change silently.
- Prices use VND. State production total and additional charges, or explicitly state that delivery is arranged and paid separately. Payments, shipping integrations, refunds, compensation and handling finished goods remain external.
- The buyer sees all complete quotations on their request. A cooperative quotation shows participants, quantities, completion dates and full buyer price. Internal contribution prices are private to the contributing household and administration. Contributions are distinct from complete quotations.
- Representatives see only their own invitations, quotations, contribution history, allocation and progress. Buyers/admins see household and total order progress. Quotation content never reaches guests, public pages, QR pages, search or an assistant. Notifications respect those audiences. Earlier administrative access rules remain.
- Recheck every supplying household at acceptance: approved, not suspended, representative not locked. Acting accounts must also be permitted. After acceptance suspension still permits existing private confirmation/progress; locking prevents representative actions. Production cannot start with a locked participating representative. Wait for unlock or cancel; administrators cannot fabricate household actions.

### Confirmation, production and exceptions

- Acceptance means awaiting household confirmation. Direct orders have one proposed allocation; cooperative orders have their fixed shares. All must confirm before production. The sole household starts a direct order; the assigned administrator starts a cooperative order.
- Declining a proposed allocation cancels the whole unstarted order, preserves the decline and accepted plan, cancels other unfinished shares and notifies participants. There is no substitution or household reassignment. Invitation refusal or no response before acceptance does not cancel a request.
- Before production the buyer or an administrator can cancel the whole request/order with a reason. Discarding an unsent draft retains the no-reason exception. A confirmed household asks for administrator cancellation rather than silently withdrawing.
- Representatives report completed quantity between zero and allocated quantity, with optional notes/photos. Corrections retain the earlier report and require a reason. Allocation completion requires full quantity. Reports stay private and do not automatically create products or publish production journals.
- Show a progress table, household dates and total completed units divided by order quantity. Flag unfinished shares after their promised dates. Omit automatic allocation strategies, Gantt charts and predicted-lateness displays.
- All allocations done means awaiting receipt, not delivered. The buyer confirms receipt, or an administrator records it on behalf of the buyer with a written explanation.
- After production starts, only an administrator can cancel an unfulfillable whole order with a reason. Keep completed quantities, finished allocations and history; cancel unfinished allocations. The order ends cancelled, never delivered. Lateness alone keeps production active with an overdue warning. Replacement work needs a new request.

### States and invariants

Retain RFQ/order states DRAFT, SENT, BIDDING, ACCEPTED, IN_PRODUCTION, DELIVERED, CANCELLED and EXPIRED. The first complete quotation opens BIDDING; contribution offers alone do not. ACCEPTED displays awaiting confirmations. All allocations done derives awaiting receipt without another required persisted state.

Retain quotation states SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, WITHDRAWN and LAPSED, with version history. Expiry/cancellation lapses open offers; an accepted quotation stays as evidence if its order cancels. Retain allocation states PROPOSED, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and CANCELLED, with the whole-order consequences above.

A request yields at most one accepted quotation and one order. Acceptance atomically checks authorization, deadline, current quotation/contribution versions, full quantity, dates, prices and eligibility. Competing acceptances yield one winner. Retries never duplicate orders, allocations or progress events. A racing contribution change either invalidates an offer first or cannot alter an accepted plan. Cancellation, confirmation, start and receipt also check fresh states; no late update may affect a cancelled order. Architecture chooses transaction and retry mechanisms.

### Concrete scenarios

1. Direct: 300 cups at 35,000 VND total 10,500,000 VND. Accept before deadline, confirm the allocation, then start. Reporting 120 cups shows 40 percent. All 300 complete still requires receipt confirmation.
2. Cooperative: 5,000 logo cups within one month. Private contributions of 2,000 at 30,000 VND, 1,500 at 32,000 VND and 1,500 at 34,000 VND total 159,000,000 VND. The buyer sees shares/dates/total, not internal rates. All confirm before administrator start. Reports of 1,000, 600 and 400 cups show 40 percent overall.
3. Contributions totalling 4,800 cannot produce a 5,000-cup offer. Withdrawing an input makes its cooperative offer unavailable. An allocation decline cancels the whole unstarted order. Concurrent acceptance creates one order. Acceptance at the deadline fails even before expiry processing.

title: Define production journals and traceability guarantees
description:
## Question

What does a production journal record, what can a visitor learn or verify through its QR page, and what rules preserve that promise?

Use the agreed object or batch identity and approval rules. Decide how an artisan records stages, timestamps, notes, and images; whether stages can repeat or be missing; what may be published before completion; and how mistakes are corrected. Specify the distinction between an informal household story and evidence tied to an identified product. Cover invalid codes, incomplete journals, unpublished or withdrawn products, changed images, and locked households.

The current web app computes a real hash chain over sample entries, but persistence and authoritative verification are unbuilt. Decide whether the proposed append-only chain belongs in this release, what changes it detects, what it cannot prove, and how the UI states those limits without claiming that a hash proves who physically made an object. Resolve the QR-link and publication lifecycle as product behavior. The answer should provide the journal rules and visitor-facing trust contract, not a hashing implementation.
notes: Prerequisite: [Define approval, publishing, and access rules](vCRAFT-9hg.3). Read its resolution and the linked scope and identity decisions before working this question.

comments.text:
## Resolution
The human accepted the recommendations in Q1 through Q7 during the live discussion on 29 October 2026. Q5 was restated by Q7 after a conflict with the approval resolution surfaced. These decisions define the journal rules and the visitor-facing trust contract for the first release. Canonical vocabulary is recorded in root GLOSSARY.md.
### What a journal records
- A production journal belongs to exactly one product, which identifies one object or one production batch. The journal is evidence of the published account of making that product. The household profile and artisan stories are informal narrative and carry no integrity claim.
- A journal entry records one stage, the date the household declares the work happened, a note, and optional images. The system also records when the entry was saved. The QR page shows the declared date as the story date and uses the system time for ordering and correction history. Backdated and future declared dates are allowed and shown exactly as declared.
- The stage vocabulary is the fixed set of seven ceramic stages: clay, throw, dry, paint, glaze, fire, finish. A stage may repeat and a stage may be skipped, but a skipped stage requires one line of reason in its entry. There are no free-text stages in the first release.
### Corrections and integrity
- Before first publication the representative edits entries freely. After publication no entry is edited or deleted silently. A mistake is fixed by a correction entry that names the entry it supersedes, and the QR page shows the original and the correction together.
- An image changed after publication follows the same rule. The old image hash stays in the published history and the replacement arrives as a correction entry.
- The first release keeps the existing SHA-256 append-only hash chain. It detects a change, deletion, or reordering of published entries. It does not prove the events happened as written and it does not prove who physically made the object. The QR page states this in one fixed sentence beside the seal, using the term Journal integrity. A broken chain names the entry that failed and links to it.
### Publication and failure behavior
- A journal is never public on its own. It appears only with its published product and is withdrawn with that product.
- An unfinished journal may be published. The QR page labels it in progress and names the stages not yet recorded.
- An invalid code, an unpublished product, a withdrawn product, and a suspended household all return the same missing page as a bad link.
- Locking the representative account freezes the household's journals. Published pages stay visible, and no new entries or corrections can be added until the lock clears. Locking hides nothing and is not a suspension.
### Follow-through within the existing map
- Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction decides how the journal timeline, the in-progress label, the correction display, and the integrity sentence are presented.
- Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries translates these rules into persistence and verification contracts. This ticket does not prescribe a hashing implementation.
No new decision ticket is needed from this resolution. The map's unshaped questions and out-of-scope boundaries are unchanged.

description:

Certificate verification covers one declared certificate and is not product authentication. Journal integrity means the household's account was not silently rewritten, not that the events happened as written. The exhibition never says approval, a verified certificate, or a QR code proves the object in hand was made by the household. The course review packet is labeled sample data: declared name, craft, workshop location, workshop photos, and a fictional village confirmation. No national identity documents.

One household representative acts for one household and is not made a maker by doing so. A named artisan without that account cannot act. comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted the recommendations in Q1 through Q9 during the live discussion. These decisions define who may act, what each approval claims, and what each audience sees in the first release. Canonical vocabulary is recorded in root GLOSSARY.md.

### Actors and accounts

- One account holds one role. A person who both buys and represents a household uses two accounts. The demo does not switch roles inside one session.
- A guest has no account and sees only published public pages.
- A buyer registers, verifies their email, and then acts only on their own quotation records.
- One household representative account acts for exactly one household. The representative may or may not be a maker. Acting never makes the representative a maker, and a named artisan without this account cannot act.
- A village administrator account is created as sample data, not by public signup. An administrator is not a member of any household and is not credited as a maker for editing or approving something.
- A household enters review in two ways, and both land in the same queue. The representative applies, or an administrator invites the representative. The invite creates the account only. It never approves the household.

### What each approval claims

Four claims stay separate in the public language.

- Household approval means the village administration accepts the household as a craft-producing unit presented in the exhibition. It is the only gate into the public exhibition and into quotation participation. It does not mean every public sentence is true, and it does not mean a named artisan made any particular object.
- Certificate verification means an administrator reviewed one certificate the household declared. An unverified certificate never appears, even on an approved profile. A verified certificate is shown as reviewed, not as proof that a product is genuine.
- Journal integrity means the household's published account of making a product was not silently replaced. It does not mean the events happened as written. How edits are recorded belongs to Define production journals and traceability guarantees.
- Physical authenticity is never claimed. Approval, a verified certificate, and a QR code do not prove that the object in someone's hand was made by this household. The QR code opens the published account of that product.

The course review packet is sample data, clearly labeled as such: the household's declared name, craft, and workshop location, workshop photos, and a fictional village confirmation. It includes no national identity documents or real identity numbers. Approving that packet means accepted into the exhibition.

### Review states

A household application is pending review, needs information, approved, or rejected.

- Nothing is public before approval. Pending review, needs information, and rejected keep the household and its documents private to the household and the administration.
- Needs information means the administration named what is missing. The household edits and resubmits, which returns the same record to pending review.
- Rejected means the administration declined the application with a written reason. The household can correct and reapply, which opens a new review of the same household record.
- Approved is one decision on the whole household, not a separate decision per page. It opens the public profile and quotation participation together.

### Who authors, and who only gates

- The representative authors their own household's story, workshops, products, journals, and certificate declarations. Drafts stay private until published.
- The administration never rewrites a household's story, journal, or bid. It approves the household, marks individual certificates verified, suspends or restores the public presence, and publishes village news. It also authors cooperative bids and coordination plans.
- The buyer authors only their own quotation requests.
- Locking an account stops that account from acting at all, including on private drafts. It does not delete or publish anything, and it is not a suspension.

### What each audience sees

- The household profile, its stories, its workshops, its certificates, and its products appear only while the household is approved.
- A production journal appears only with its published product and is withdrawn with that product.
- Public news shows to everyone. Household-only news shows to representatives of approved households and to administrators. For a guest, a buyer, or anyone else, a direct link is treated as not existing.
- A buyer sees their own requests and every bid on them. A household sees only its own invitations, its own bids and their history, and its own share of coordinated work. One household never sees another household's prices. An administrator sees all quotation records because coordination needs them. A guest sees none.
- No quotation content appears on public pages, in public search, or in the assistant's answers. A buyer who asks for village-level coordination shares that request with the assigned administrator only, and that consent covers coordination, not publication.

### Failure behavior

- When the audience rule is about secrecy, the product hides existence. A guest or buyer opening household-only news, a private draft, or another household's bid gets the same missing page as a bad link. A representative opening the review queue, coordination screens, or another household's records gets the same missing page.
- When the rule is about permission, the product refuses with a reason. Editing another household's product or bidding after the deadline returns 403, and the screen explains the rule in plain words.
- Rejection changes nothing public, because nothing public existed.
- Suspension hides the public profile, all products, and all workshops from listings, the map, and search. Existing QR codes and saved links stay scannable and open a short unavailable notice. They do not show the old story, and they do not pretend the address was always empty. Private quotation drafts and history stay visible to their owners and to administrators. While suspended, the representative cannot publish, edit public pages, or place a new bid. Ending suspension restores what was hidden without a new review, unless the administration separately requires one.
- Withdrawing one product hides that product and its journal, and its QR code opens the same unavailable notice. The rest of the household stays public.
- A workshop's own temporarily-closed flag marks only that workshop. The pin shows closed, the page states the reason and when it may reopen, and the household and its products stay public. Closing one workshop never triggers a review, and suspension never rewrites a workshop's own open or closed flag.

### Follow-through within the existing map

- Define production journals and traceability guarantees decides how a journal records edits so the integrity claim above can be kept.
- Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules decides quantities, allocations, and progress inside the audience rules above.
- Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction decides how an approved profile, a verified certificate, and the unavailable notice are presented.
- Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries translates these actor, state, and audience rules into contracts. This ticket does not implement authentication or policies.

No new decision ticket is needed from this resolution.

comments.text:
## Resolution

The human accepted the recommendations in Q1, Q2-Q4, and Q5-Q8 during the live discussion. These decisions define the first-release domain relationships. Canonical vocabulary is recorded in root GLOSSARY.md.

### Household, artisan, and representation

- Household is the craft-producing unit presented under its own public name and history. It is the main public identity and can include several artisans.
- Artisan is an individual maker associated with a household. An artisan's name, contribution, and personal story can be distinguished from the household's collective history.
- Each household has one designated representative account for the first release, and that account represents one household. The representative may be an artisan or someone handling administration. Named artisans do not need accounts to receive credit.
- Household identity is independent of the representative account. Managing an account or uploading a journal does not automatically make someone a maker of the product.
- Every Product has one responsible Household. It may credit several artisans and their contributions, or credit the household's makers collectively when individual names are not supplied. Outside assistance can be acknowledged in the story while one household remains responsible.

Example: Gốm An is the household. Bình shapes a vase and Lan paints it, so both can receive maker credit. Another family member manages the account and uploads their account of the work without being presented as the vase's maker.

### Workshops and visiting

- Workshop is a physical craft location listed under a household. One household can list several workshops, each with its own location and visiting information.
- Map inclusion does not imply permission to enter. A production site and a place that welcomes visitors are distinct facts.
- A Product can name several production workshops of its responsible household. Its suggested visiting location is selected separately from a household location that welcomes visitors.

Example: Gốm An shapes a vase at one workshop, fires it at another, and welcomes visitors at its showroom. The production history names the production locations, while visitor directions lead to the showroom.

### Product identity, batches, and designs

- Each Product identifies one physical object or one specific Production batch. It has its own production history, journal, and QR code.
- A Production batch contains objects of one design made during one defined production run. A later run gets another Product identity even when the design is unchanged.
- Objects in a batch can share the batch's QR code. That code identifies the shared batch history rather than individually distinguishing every object within it.
- The number of objects represented by a batch is distinct from available stock. Selling or allocating some objects does not change which objects the batch identifies.
- Product design describes the repeatable appearance and characteristics shared by objects or batches. For the first release it remains descriptive information on each Product, which may be reused for a later batch. There is no separately managed design catalogue.

Examples: a unique vase is one Product representing one object. A March run of 300 blue cups is one Product representing a batch, and an April run of 200 cups of the same design is another Product with its own journal and QR code. Allocating 20 March cups does not redefine the March batch as 280 cups.

### Comparison with the assignment and current proposals

The binding assignment, docs/requirements/vCraft.pdf pages 2-4, requires household/workshop stories, product journals and QR storytelling, workshop visitor information, and wholesale work shared across households. It does not define a batch or separate household identity from a named maker.

The accepted model resolves these ambiguities in the proposals and demo:

- docs/SRS.md:50 merges household and artisan. apps/web/src/lib/demo/data.ts:33 combines a household name, one artisan name, and one workshop location in a single Artisan type. These concepts must remain distinct under the agreed vocabulary.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:375 already allows several workshops per household profile, but the demo flattens the location and the proposed trace response at docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:462 names a single workshop. Later contracts must preserve production locations separately from the visiting destination.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:405 attaches one trace code to a Product with stock, without defining object versus batch identity. The demo includes a 300-stock cup product with one code. That shared code is meaningful under the accepted model only when it identifies a particular production batch, not all future repetitions of a design.
- The proposed account-to-profile relationship does not replace Household identity, and the existing single artisan-name display is insufficient to express several makers' contributions.

### Follow-through within the existing map

- [Define approval, publishing, and access rules](vCRAFT-9hg.3) decides onboarding, permissions, and publication using the agreed representative relationship.
- [Define production journals and traceability guarantees](vCRAFT-9hg.4) decides journal timing, corrections, evidence, and QR lifecycle for the agreed object-or-batch identity. This resolution does not claim that a QR code proves who physically made an object.
- [Define quotation and shared-order coordination rules](vCRAFT-9hg.5) decides quotation quantities, allocations, and progress. The batch count and available quantity must remain distinct concepts.
- [Choose the exhibition journey, content, and visual direction](vCRAFT-9hg.6) decides presentation of household history, maker credit, production locations, and visitor directions.
- [Choose the technical architecture and reuse boundaries](vCRAFT-9hg.7) translates these relationships into contracts and persistence. This ticket does not prescribe tables or execute migrations.

No new decision ticket is needed from this resolution. The remaining questions belong to the existing named decisions. The map's unshaped questions and out-of-scope boundaries are unchanged.
